video_title: Micah Nori Postgame Interview | Trail Blazers 124, Suns 83 | Oct. 21, 2026

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on team performance and execution in season opener
quotes.excerpt: The guys came out, competed, Mike Williams' game plan was right on point and the guys just executed.
quotes.quote: It's exactly what we thought we were going to do was come out and go on a 20-0 run to start the season. But in all seriousness, the guys came out, competed, Mike Williams' game plan was right on point and the guys just executed. We talked about it and we talked about it in here about physicality, making sure we took care of the basketball and the possession game and I think that first quarter, I might be wrong, I think we had maybe allowed one offensive rebound, no turnovers, but I know we had no points off of either.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori praised the team's execution in the season opener, noting the focus on physicality and ball security. He credited the game plan for a strong start that saw the team limit turnovers and offensive rebounds early on.

structured.context: Micah Nori discusses the team's performance and execution during the season opener against the Phoenix Suns.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on defensive physicality and challenging opposing stars
quotes.excerpt: Jaylen Green and obviously Devin Booker provided a lot of challenges, especially when we do start a little bit small.
quotes.quote: I thought all the guys, especially just from the start of the game, we talked about being physical up the floor with our line of scrimmage. Jaylen Green and obviously Devin Booker provided a lot of challenges, especially when we do start a little bit small. But I thought that all the way around, guarded them very, very well. To my got two fouls, we were able to get City in and kind of still hold water if you will. But Rob's physicality was great, but just from the get-go, that starting five I thought really set the tone.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori highlighted the defensive effort against Devin Booker and Jaylen Green, noting that the starting five set the tone for the game with their physicality up the floor.

structured.context: Micah Nori reflects on the team's defensive physicality against opposing stars Jaylen Green and Devin Booker.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on team playmaking and reducing reliance on one player
quotes.excerpt: I think the one thing that helps Dame is he doesn't have to bring it up and play pick and roll.
quotes.quote: I think the one thing that helps Dame is he doesn't have to bring it up and play pick and roll. And very much so, I mean this like same as Denny as well last year. A lot of times Denny had to bring it up and had to carry a lot, especially when the injuries bug struck. So I think with Ja and with Denny and obviously we know what Dame can do with the basketball, but just being able to not have one guy just bring it up and play pick and roll, but to be able to get those guys off the ball, get them in a closeout situation where they can attack downhill. I mean, Denny is as good as anybody in the league at getting to the free throw line and getting downhill as we saw. And then anytime you give Dame any bit of air space, he's going to knock one down.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says the goal for the offense is to reduce the burden on Dame by utilizing secondary playmakers. He noted that getting guys off the ball allows them to attack downhill and creates better spacing for the team.

structured.context: Micah Nori explains the offensive strategy of distributing playmaking duties among Damian Lillard, Deni Avdija, and Ja Morant.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on Dame's role as a screener in the offense
quotes.excerpt: Dame is really good screener and a lot of times with setting the rip screens and that type of stuff.
quotes.quote: I think the one thing that we've done, Dame is really good screener and a lot of times with setting the rip screens and that type of stuff, they have to make a decision. Do they switch and then maybe they lose a little bit of space or whatever with Dame? And so I think that to put him in different situations has been good for him and good for us.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori highlighted Dame's role as a screener in the new offense, noting that using him in different situations forces defenses to make difficult decisions on switches.

structured.context: Micah Nori discusses utilizing Damian Lillard as a screener to create spacing and tactical advantages for the offense.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on Ja's competitive growth and defensive impact
quotes.excerpt: He's competing at the highest level now because he knows that he's on a team that has a chance.
quotes.quote: I think it will look like, like we talk about and I know it's just one game and the sample size is very, very small, but I think that he's competing. He's competing at the highest level now because he knows that he's on a team that has a chance to win some basketball games. And I'm not saying that he didn't compete in Memphis, but I know that he was hurt, but you know, he's still a young guy and I think that he is going to show everyone exactly who he is and he's not trying to do anything more than he has to or he needs to. But I thought he did a great job. I thought he was very physical on the defensive end and trying to do it there and then made all the right plays. He puts pressure on the defense downhill, very good passer as we saw, and even with his late passes and his lob stuff that he's seeing late to Rob.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori praised the competitive growth of Ja, noting his defensive impact and ability to make the right plays. He believes Ja is competing at a high level now that he is on a team with a chance to win.

structured.context: Micah Nori evaluates Ja Morant's competitive growth and defensive impact following his first game with the team.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on Tumani's shooting development and spacing impact
quotes.excerpt: His catch and shoot threes in our practice facility since labor days like 52%.
quotes.quote: His catch and shoot threes in our practice facility since labor days like 52%. So I don't think it's an aberration, but absolutely. And again, I hate to keep going back to, but this is what we talked about and what we knew. When you have decision makers and you got guys can draw a crowd and obviously the magnitude that which Dame pulls guys when he's off the ball, Tumani and those guys are going to get nice open looks. I thought Scoot, even though he was one for five in the first half, I thought every single one of those were good looks as well. But I think that absolutely. Tumani, even City, and these guys are going to be able to catch and shoot, shoot all of them, quite honestly. I hope they do.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori is confident in the shooting development of his role players, citing high practice percentages. He expects Tumani and others to continue getting open looks as defenses are forced to focus on Dame.

structured.context: Micah Nori discusses the shooting development of Tumani Camara and the spacing benefits provided by Damian Lillard.
